messages:
maya: Heads-up — deploy-bot just paused the publish to ECR for runtime image. I saw a provenance attestation mismatch on the multi-arch manifest.

deploy-bot: Automated action: publish blocked for image gcr.redwood/dev/runtime:v2026-03-20-rc3 (manifest: sha256:aaa...111). Reason: provenance.attestation.subjectDigest != manifest.digest. See CI job 4872.

dmitri: hmm, did the builder push a new manifest after attest? Could be a manifest-level recompose for arm64.

ana: @maya is this the one that went through cross-build matrix last night? We had a retry step that may have re-uploaded a layer.

maya: yes @ana — matrix job 20260319-21 had a retry on amd64 layer. The attestation was signed before retry.

kerim: if it's only the digest mismatch we can either: 1) re-run attestation after the final push, or 2) pin the deploy to the known-good digest and roll out that digest instead of the tag. Which is lower risk during the change window?

sre-oncall: rolling in the middle of the EU morning slack window is okay but we should avoid a full rollback if unnecessary. pin-to-digest + small canary seems safest.

maya: Agree. Plan: pin to sha256:bbb...222 (the attested digest) in the release job, skip tag aliasing for the moment, and re-run the signing job on the composite manifest. @infra-bot can you queue a reattestation job?

infra-bot: Queued job 4890 -> reattest-manifest for manifest sha256:aaa...111. Expected duration ~4m. No infra changes required.

deploy-bot: Note: current tag v2026-03-20-rc3 is blocked. Canary rollout queued with image digest sha256:bbb...222 on pool "dedicated-gpu-3". Will auto-fallback to previous stable if latency errors > 5% or error rate > 2% within 5m.

dmitri: If reattest fails, we should retag the final manifest to a temporary tag and update the release notes so customers on Dedicated don't get surprise alias changes. Also we need to add a CI check to ensure attest happens after final push in matrix.

ana: filing RFC now for pushing attest step after the final manifest compose: https://go/release/rfcs/attest-after-compose (draft).

maya: For immediate action: @kerim can you update release pipeline to pin digest and start canary? I'll watch job 4872 and 4890.

kerim: On it — running `./scripts/release/pin_and_deploy --digest sha256:bbb...222 --canary 1%` now.

infra-bot: Job 4890 completed: reattestation result = success. Attestation subjectDigest matches manifest sha256:aaa...111 AFTER compose.

maya: Wait — attestation now matches aaa...111 but canary is pinned to bbb...222. Is there a stray duplicate manifest?

dmitri: Looks like builder produced two distinct manifests with different canonical ordering; digest bbb...222 corresponds to the attested image originally recorded. The new compose produced aaa...111. We need to unify to a single canonical manifest.

kerim: To avoid confusion I'm pausing canary deployment. `pin_and_deploy` output: canary paused due to digest drift.

maya: Ok rollback plan: revert to previous stable tag (v2026-03-19-hotfix -> digest sha256:ccc...333) for the next 30m maintenance window while we fix compose/sign ordering. I'll post release notes update. @sre-oncall please approve emergency pin.

sre-oncall: Approved. Will monitor. If anything spikes, hit me on call.

ana: Next steps capture: 1) fix CI ordering (attest after final compose), 2) add manifest canonicalization step to compose tool, 3) add a lint that compares attested digest to final manifest before releasing tag aliasing. I'll open PRs.

maya: Thanks all. I'll update the release doc and send a short note to #customer-notify if we need to extend the change window.

kerim: PRs incoming: compose-canonicalize (MR 1127), ci-attest-order (MR 1128). Leaving this thread open until retagging and rollback are complete.

deploy-bot: Action summary: publish blocked -> canary queued -> canary paused -> emergency pin to v2026-03-19-hotfix applied.

maya: Closing thread once we've confirmed traffic on pinned digest stable for 15m.

infra-bot: Traffic stable on pinned digest (15m). No error spikes. Thread can be closed. :white_check_mark:
